Chernivtsi Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Chernivtsi (Vinnytsia Oblast), founded in 1383, saw Jewish settlement from the early 17th century, reaching 2,274 of 8,994 residents (25 percent) by 1897; many town Jews lived in poverty, with 60 families receiving charitable fuel assistance in 1898 alone. The community notably escaped pogroms during the 1919–20 Russian Civil War. A ghetto established after the mid-1941 German-Romanian occupation held about 1,500 local Jews and several hundred Bessarabian and Bukovinian deportees, repeatedly saved from planned Aktions through bribes paid to the Romanian administration. This cemetery holds at least 3,000 graves dating from the late 19th to 20th centuries.
